Yet the workflow has the `artifact-metadata: write` ([amongst all the other required permissions](https://github.com/actions/attest-build-provenance/blob/00014ed6ed5efc5b1ab7f7f34a39eb55d41aa4f8/README.md?plain=1#L46-L49)) enabled:


```
  docker-attest:
    name: Attest Docker container
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      artifact-metadata: write
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
      packages: write
    needs:
      - docker-build
      - docker-publish
    # Check if the event is not triggered by a fork
    if: |
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - name: Set up Docker
        uses: docker/setup-docker-action@e61617a16c407a86262fb923c35a616ddbe070b3 # v4.6.0
        with:
          daemon-config: |
            {
              "features": {
                "containerd-snapshotter": true
              }
            }
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3.12.0

      - name: Log into registry ${{ needs.docker-build.outputs.registry }}
        uses: docker/login-action@5e57cd118135c172c3672efd75eb46360885c0ef # v3.6.0
        with:
          registry: ${{ needs.docker-build.outputs.registry }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # note that we use the digest of the local image
      # these digests don't change after pushing, but
      # since we deal with tags (mutable), and the way to get a digest is to use the tag, I prefer
      # sourcing the digest from the local registry we just spun up (trusted)
      - name: Generate artifact attestation
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@00014ed6ed5efc5b1ab7f7f34a39eb55d41aa4f8 # v3.1.0
        id: attestation
        with:
          subject-name: ${{ needs.docker-build.outputs.full_image_name_remote_registry }}
          subject-digest: ${{ needs.docker-publish.outputs.digest }}
          push-to-registry: true
```

comments.body: Thanks for the report, we are looking into this.

Is there documentation / examples somewhere to be found what to expect when this would work? I can't find anything about what an artifact metadata storage record actually is? Is it the creation of this https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/artifact-metadata?apiVersion=2022-11-28#create-artifact-metadata-storage-record automated in the action as well?

Is it the creation of this https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/artifact-metadata?apiVersion=2022-11-28#create-artifact-metadata-storage-record automated in the action as well?

Yes, when this option is enabled and working as expected, the artifact metadata storage record described in the API docs you linked to will be created. Thanks for bringing the documentation gap to our attention, we will add some more information to the README on this.

@kristof-mattei currently storage records can only be created on behalf of repositories owned by organizations. The shared logs seem to indicate the repository is owned by your user instead of an organization. This would explain why you still received a 404 response after including the `artifact_metadata:write` permission. We are working on documentation to close the communication gap and a fix to prevent these warning logs from appearing for a user owned repositories.

[v3.2.0](https://github.com/actions/attest-build-provenance/releases/tag/v3.2.0) has been released. With this version, you should no longer see warning logs related to storage records and the `artifact_metadata:write` permission when using the Action with the `push-to-registry` option set to true on a user owned repository.
I will close this as resolved with the new release but please reach out if another issue arises.
